claims.text: The name Tulkastor is in Qenya. Its meaning is unclear, but it appears to contain the name of the Vala Tulkas (from the root TULUK-, meaning "steady, firm").
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Sí Qente Feanor and Other Elvish Writings", in Parma Eldalamberon XV (edited by Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, Patrick H. Wynne, and Bill Welden), p. 10

claims.text:
The Gnomish cognate of Tulkastor is Tulchathron.
Originally the name of the character was Turenbor, later changed to Tulkassë and finally to Tulkastor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Sí Qente Feanor and Other Elvish Writings", in Parma Eldalamberon XV (edited by Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, Patrick H. Wynne, and Bill Welden), p. 7; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part One, "I. The Cottage of Lost Play": "Notes and Commentary", p. 22
